title: Larger Courtland Avenue and Park Street towers approved with affordable housing
subtitle: Inclusionary zoning, community centre model, e-bikes on trails, lived expertise group deferral, GO train advocacy and planning law changes
overview: Council approved two large downtown-area developments after the applicants increased height and density and added affordable housing at the meeting. The Courtland Avenue East site (the former Schneider site) gained units, more front-loaded affordable units and a larger cash contribution to the Working Centre. A 42-storey tower at Park Street and Victoria Street South was approved with 30 affordable units for 25 years and a lower parking rate.

Council also adopted a modernized community centre model for neighbourhood associations, including expanded fee assistance and inclusion support. It directed staff to continue work on inclusionary zoning {{vote:m21}}, approved planning changes responding to provincial legislation including two more planning staff, and allowed Neuron e-bikes on multi-use trails.

Funding for the Lived Expertise Working Group was deferred to August 28, with funding continuing in the meantime. Council also asked staff to develop a Community Benefits Charge strategy, endorsed advocacy for more GO train service, and backed three FCM resolutions on mental health, homelessness and municipal finance.

decisions.item: Courtland Avenue East subdivision and plan amendments
decisions.detail: Council gave draft plan approval and adopted the amended official plan and zoning changes for the Courtland Ave E, Palmer Ave and Vernon Ave site, with the applicant's revised density, height and affordable housing offer.

decisions.item: Park Street and Victoria Street South tower
decisions.detail: Council adopted the official plan and zoning amendments, as amended, for a mixed-use tower at 97-101 Park Street and 186-194 Victoria Street South.

decisions.item: Lived Expertise Working Group year two
decisions.detail: Council deferred the year-two funding decision to August 28, 2023 to allow further discussion with the working group and its partner organization, with funding continuing under the existing agreement.
Council approved, as amended, expanded fee assistance and inclusion support for neighbourhood association programs, new affiliation conditions, and a review of weekend and extended hours.
Staff were directed to use the discussion paper for further consultation and to draft inclusionary zoning policy and zoning by-law amendments with the neighbouring municipalities and the Region.
Council adopted official plan, zoning, site plan, demolition control and delegation by-law changes responding to Bills 13, 109 and 23, and added two planning staff positions.
Staff were directed to amend the Neuron Mobility agreement so e-bikes may use surfaced multi-use trails like e-scooters, with a temporary by-law exemption.
Staff were directed to develop a Community Benefits Charge strategy and by-law.

debate: On the Courtland site, one councillor asked why only 10 of about 640 added units were affordable; the applicant's planner said the affordable share fell slightly but units were front-loaded, with 53 starting in July, plus a larger cash contribution.

A delegate supported the Courtland plan but urged lower-carbon construction such as avoiding gas heating; the planner could not say what systems would be used. Another councillor noted geothermal had been ruled out.

On Growing Together, delegates asked for a defined meaning of appropriate transitions in height, more low- and mid-rise options, and better engagement, citing a crowded library workshop. Staff said work on transitions was continuing and would come back in December.

On the Lived Expertise Working Group, staff said a funding agreement clause on public statements about the City had not been fully followed, while the delegate said requests to meet were unanswered. Some councillors preferred deferral to allow talks.
On Neuron e-bikes, some councillors worried about safety on busy trails and wanted signage first; supporters said the bikes are speed-limited to 15 km/h and the pilot would provide data.
